352263.title: Effective asymmetric coloring conjecture for inverse limits of finite permutation groups
352263.literal_statement:
Let $\mathscr{Gr}$ denote the class of finite permutation groups. Let $(G_i,\varphi_i)_{i\leq k}$ be an epimorphic inverse sequence of length $k$ of finite permutation groups with pairwise disjoint domains. A coloring is **zero-neutral** and **zero-asymmetric** in the sense used for the inverse-limit action in the paper.

**Effective asymmetric coloring conjecture.** There exists a function $g:\mathscr{Gr}\to\mathbb N$ such that, whenever $k\geq g(G_0)$, the inverse limit of this system admits a zero-neutral zero-asymmetric 2-coloring.

The preceding finite theorem proves a bound depending on an intermediate group $G_c$; this conjecture asks for a bound depending only on the initial group $G_0$. The given text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

346529.title: The TVK-shape sorting-probability conjecture
346529.literal_statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge 2$. Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R^d_{>0}$ be a Thoma sequence, let $\lambda\simeq \alpha n$ be a TVK $\alpha$-shape, and let $P_\lambda$ be the associated Young-diagram poset. Let $\delta(P_\lambda)$ denote its sorting probability.

**TVK-shape sorting-probability conjecture.** There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\delta(P_\lambda)\le \frac{C}{n^{5/4}}.
$$

The paper proves an $O(n^{-1/2})$ upper bound in this setting and suggests that it is not tight. The conjectured $n^{-5/4}$ rate remains open.

347305.title: Mubayi–Verstraëte's Steiner-system extremal conjecture for 3-graphs
347305.literal_statement:
Let $m\ge4$ and let $n$ be sufficiently large. Suppose that $\mathcal{H}\subset\binom{[n]}{3}$ contains no non-trivial intersecting family of size $3m+1$. A **Steiner $(n,3,m-1)$-system** is a $3$-graph on $n$ vertices in which every pair of vertices is contained in exactly $m-1$ edges. **Mubayi–Verstraëte's conjecture.** Then

$$
|\mathcal{H}|\le\frac{m-1}{3}\binom{n}{2},
$$

with equality if and only if $\mathcal{H}$ is a Steiner $(n,3,m-1)$-system. The conjecture is refuted: the paper constructs, for the relevant parameters, a $3$-graph with more edges that still contains no non-trivial intersecting subgraph of size $3m+1$.

343596.title: Kneser graph packing conjecture
343596.literal_statement:
For integers $n>k\geq 1$, let $\operatorname{KG}(n,k)$ be the graph whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of $[n]$, with two vertices adjacent exactly when the corresponding sets are disjoint. Two copies are **packed** into a graph when their edge sets are placed on the same vertex set without overlap. **Kneser graph packing conjecture.** If two copies of $\operatorname{KG}(n,k)$ can be packed into the complete graph on $\binom{n}{k}=N$ vertices, then

$$
k=\Omega(n).
$$

The paper proves only the weaker lower bound $k=\Omega(n/(\log n)^2)$ under the same packing hypothesis. The linear lower bound is presented as an open question related to the sunflower conjecture.

343641.title: Weighted Aldous–Lyons soficity conjecture
343641.literal_statement:
Let $\alpha:\Gamma\curvearrowright (X,\mu)$ be a nonsingular action of a finitely generated group with symmetric generating system $\Sigma$. For each $\sigma\in\Sigma$, suppose

$$
\frac{1}{K}\leq R(\sigma,x)\leq K.
$$

**Weighted Aldous–Lyons soficity conjecture.** There exists a sequence of $K$-weighted graphs ${G_n,p_n}_{n=1}^\infty$ such that $\alpha$ is the limit of ${G_n,p_n}_{n=1}^\infty$.

This is the weighted version of the Aldous–Lyons “Soficity” conjecture: every suitably bounded nonsingular action should arise as the weighted Benjamini–Schramm limit of finite weighted graphs. The source presents it as the converse to the fact that every convergent sequence of weighted graphs admits a limit action; its resolution status is not specified here.

344405.title: Near-perfect matching conjecture for 5-connected 1-planar graphs
344405.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a 5-connected 1-planar graph with $n$ vertices. A matching is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges.

**Near-perfect matching conjecture.** Every 5-connected 1-planar graph has a matching of size

$$
\frac{n}{2}-O(1).
$$

The claim is motivated by a construction of 5-connected 1-planar graphs whose independent stellation-vertices force at least two unmatched vertices in every matching, while the graphs otherwise have near-perfect matchings. Whether higher connectivity generally implies Hamiltonicity in all 1-planar graphs remains an open question.

353154.title: Chen–Wu–An conjecture on minimum total distance of graphs with given radius
353154.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $W(G)$ denote the sum of distances between all unordered pairs of vertices. For positive integers $n$ and $r$ satisfying $n\ge 2r$ and $r\ge 3$, let $G_{n,r,s}$ be the graph defined in the paper by blowing up two consecutive vertices of the cycle $C_{2r}$ into cliques $K_s$ and $K_{n-2r+2-s}$. **Chen–Wu–An's conjecture.** For any graph $G$ of order $n$ with radius $r$, 
$$
W(G) \ge W(G_{n,r,1}).
$$
 Equality holds if and only if $G \cong G_{n,r,s}$ where 
$$
1 \le s \le \frac{n-2r+2}{2}.
$$
 This conjecture proposes the extremal graphs minimizing total distance for fixed order and radius; the paper studies and resolves the analogous question for sufficiently large $n$ relative to $r$.

338510.title: The Sárközy–Sós conjecture for multivariate linear forms
338510.literal_statement:
Let $d\geq 1$ and let $k_1,\dots,k_d$ be positive integers. For an infinite set of positive integers $\mathcal{A}$, write $r_{\mathcal{A}}(n;k_1,\dots,k_d)$ for the number of representations of $n$ by the corresponding multivariate linear form.

**Sárközy–Sós conjecture.** There exists some infinite set of positive integers $\mathcal{A}$ such that $r_{\mathcal{A}}(n;k_1,\dots,k_d)$ is constant for $n$ large enough if and only if, up to permutation of the indices,

$$
(k_1,\dots,k_d)=(1,k,k^2,\dots,k^{d-1})
$$

for some $k\geq 2$.

The conjecture extends the known construction of Moser for coefficients $k_i=k^{i-1}$ and concerns the exceptional cases not covered by the paper's nonexistence results, including representation functions such as $r_{\mathcal{A}}(n;1,1,2)$.

340819.title: Neftin's simultaneous conjugation conjecture for permutations
340819.literal_statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be permutations in $S_n$. Write $[\alpha,\beta]=\alpha\beta\alpha^{-1}\beta^{-1}$ for their commutator, and let $\alpha^\gamma=\gamma^{-1}\alpha\gamma$ denote conjugation by $\gamma$. **Neftin's conjecture.** If $[\alpha,\beta]$ has at least $n-4$ fixed points, then there exists a permutation $\gamma\in S_n$ such that

$$
\alpha^\gamma=\alpha^{-1}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\beta^\gamma=\beta^{-1}.
$$

A positive solution would settle the hardest remaining cases in the primitive Hurwitz problem for $S_d\wr S_2$ and complete the Hurwitz part of the classification of monodromy groups for sufficiently large degrees; the parser reports that the conjecture has been resolved.

335117.title: Hefetz–Keevash's Turán conjecture for extensions of two-edge matchings
335117.literal_statement:
Let $r\geq 4$ and let $H_{2r}^{M_2^r}$ be the extension of the $r$-uniform matching $M_2^r$ consisting of two pairwise disjoint edges. Let $G$ be an $r$-graph on $[n]$, and let $S^r(n)$ be the $r$-graph whose vertex set is partitioned into $A$ and $B$, whose edges have one vertex in $A$ and $r-1$ vertices in $B$, with the part sizes chosen to maximise the number of edges. **Hefetz–Keevash's conjecture.** For sufficiently large $n$,

$$
ex(n,H_{2r}^{M_2^r})={1 \over r}n\cdot{{r-1 \over r}n \choose r-1}.
$$

Moreover, if $G$ is $H_{2r}^{M_2^r}$-free and has this many edges, then $G\cong S^r(n)$. This conjecture predicts both the exact Turán number and the unique extremal construction for the extension of a two-edge matching; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

336276.title: The random-interval sequence k-width scaling conjecture
336276.literal_statement:
Let $k\geq 2$, and let $R_n$ be a sequence of $n$ random intervals. Write $E[k\operatorname{-wd}(R_n)]$ for the expected $k$-width of $R_n$. **Random-interval sequence scaling conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $c_k>0$ such that

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{E[k\operatorname{-wd}(R_n)]}{n}=c_k,
$$

and moreover

$$
c_k=\frac{1}{k+1}.
$$

The conjecture predicts linear scaling for the $k$-width of sequences of random intervals when $k\geq 2$, contrasting with the known behavior for $k=1$. The constants are motivated by computational experiments, while the asserted limit and formula remain open.

336937.literal_statement: Let $(a(n))_{n\geq1}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. Call it **quasi-arithmetic** if it has the finite-dimensional arithmetic-progression structure defined in the source. For a real number $\alpha$, consider $(\{a(n)\alpha\})_{n\geq1}$. **Quasi-arithmetic obstruction conjecture.** If $(a(n))_{n\geq1}$ is quasi-arithmetic, then there is no $\alpha$ such that the pair correlations of $(\{a(n)\alpha\})_{n\geq1}$ are asymptotically Poissonian. This is presented as an equivalent formulation of the preceding additive-energy conjecture.

337435.title: The bounded-deficiency conjecture for graphs excluding six-vertex bipartite graphs
337435.literal_statement:
Let $\alpha(G)$ denote the stability number of a graph $G$, let $\omega(G)$ denote its clique number, and call $G$ **free of** a family of graphs if it contains none of them as an induced subgraph. Consider the family consisting of the six-vertex bipartite graphs with a perfect matching and their complements. **The bounded-deficiency conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that every graph $G$ free of this family satisfies

$$
\alpha(G)+\omega(G)\geq |V(G)|-c.
$$

This conjecture asks whether excluding these natural obstructions forces the deficiency $|V(G)|-\alpha(G)-\omega(G)$ to be bounded independently of $G$; no resolution is given in the source.

332314.title: The optimal-size clique transversal conjecture for 4-chordal graphs
332314.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a chordal graph with $n$ vertices. Call $G$ **4-chordal** if every edge of $G$ is contained in a clique with four vertices, and call a set of vertices $U$ a **clique transversal** if it meets every non-trivial maximal clique of $G$.

**Optimal-size clique transversal conjecture.** Every $4$-chordal graph with $n$ vertices has a clique transversal of size at most $2n/7$.

The question generalizes known bounds for $2$- and $3$-chordal graphs. Andreae and Flotow constructed arbitrarily large examples requiring at least $2n/7-O(1)$ vertices, suggesting that the bound is asymptotically tight; the paper proves the stronger integral bound $2(n-1)/7$ for $n\geq 5$.

332662.title: Quadratic additive bound conjecture for sparse spanning strongly connected subgraphs of tournaments
332662.literal_statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $T$ be a strongly $k$-connected tournament on $n$ vertices. A **strongly $k$-connected spanning subgraph** is a spanning subgraph with strong vertex-connectivity at least $k$. **Quadratic additive bound conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that $T$ contains a strongly $k$-connected spanning subgraph $D$ with at most

$$
kn+Ck^2
$$

arcs. The paper proves an upper bound of $kn+750k^2\log_2(k+1)$ arcs and states that reducing the additive term to $O(k^2)$ is conjectured; the supplied text gives no resolution of this conjecture.
